dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Lira! You’re being moved to the pit. Follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: *Just put in the time and you won’t have to work the pit anymore.*

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: At this point I think Kip is lying to me.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: You’d think a year would be long enough to earn some respect around here.

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Watch your head.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: You act like I’ve never done this before.

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Enough with the attitude, keep it moving!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Damn, how does the pit keep getting colder?

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Now, since you act like you can’t do your job, show me you still remember. Go pick up that heat unit over there.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Yeah, yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Now, don’t mistake this for me liking you, but I’m required to let you use ONE heat unit when working the pit.

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Good, you still remember how to use your arms. Now brake it in front of me. The council wouldn’t be happy if you kept it.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: (sigh of relief)

dialogues.speaker: Foreman
dialogues.text: And over here is “the pit,” one of the coldest places in the mine. People tend to avoid it as much as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Get over here now!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Damn, ever heard the word please?

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Now’s not the time. Stand here and shut up.

dialogues.speaker: Shaw
dialogues.text: You’re right you can really feel the temperature drop.

dialogues.speaker: Shaw
dialogues.text: And what might you have done to end up here?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Well, ever since I was young, I dreamed of breaking my back so that others could enjoy the benefits.

dialogues.speaker: Shaw
dialogues.text: (chuckles)

dialogues.speaker: Shaw
dialogues.text: We all must do our part to serve our Holy Mother.

dialogues.speaker: Shaw
dialogues.text: No matter how big or small the role we must rid ourselves of personal desire and offer our minds and bodies to the betterment of our sacred city.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: And what might YOU be offering to our so called “mother”?

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Don't ever ta...

dialogues.speaker: Shaw
dialogues.text: Forgive her, for she knows not what she does.

dialogues.speaker: Shaw
dialogues.text: The Holy Mother is not a stranger to such malevolence and will continue to serve all Her children.

dialogues.speaker: Shaw
dialogues.text: What was your name dear?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Lira.

dialogues.speaker: Shaw
dialogues.text: Remember to appreciate what you have Lira.

dialogues.speaker: Shaw
dialogues.text: When we covet more than we need, the consequences are cruel and uncertain.

dialogues.speaker: Shaw
dialogues.text: We must keep moving. There is much more to see.

dialogues.speaker: Foreman
dialogues.text: Of course, right this way sir!

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Turns out you’re a lot more of an idiot than I thought.

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Talking back to the head councillor like that. I should’ve fired you on the spot!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: And defy the forgiveness of our head councillor?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I don’t think that would go to well with you know who.

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: You think you’re so smart.

dialogues.speaker: Shift Leader
dialogues.text: Get back to work! Hit your quota or you’re gone!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I’ll get out of this mine someday.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Lira, what are those!?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: There was an explosion in the mine today so I dec…

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Why did you bring those home!?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Because I’m sick of being cold and saw an opportunity, so I took it.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Lira do you know what Shaw and the council would do to you if they found out you stole from them?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I’m just so tired of doing everything the way the council tells us to do it.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: “We provide light. We provide heat. You can rely on us.”

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: When has that ever been true?

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: You say that but they are the ONLY reason you’re able to live your life. Without them and the tower our city would be a frozen wasteland, like outside the walls.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Yeah, well if my mom were here, she’d be on my side.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Don’t pretend you knew who she was.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Well maybe I would know more about her if you didn’t pretend she never existed!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: My whole life, I’ve heard the same thing from everyone “Your mother was wonderful”, “Your mother was so kind”, “Your mother was a genius.”

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: When am I going to get a real answer, and not one you’d give to a six-year-old?

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: You’re right…

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: It’s about time you knew the truth about your mother.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Your mother wasn’t born in the outskirts.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Neither was I for that matter… we both grew up in the Core.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Clara grew up in a wealthy family that lived near the top of the Core. As she got older, Clara found an interest in science, fascinated by the tower and how it could sustain life after centuries without a real sun.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: This lead to her pursue science and further her education.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Clara met your father, Reginald Brown this way.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: My… father?

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Yes, he was your father.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: They were inseparable; studying, partying, you name it. Her success in school allowed her to land a job working in the Primary Tower Lab as soon as she graduated.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Clara became the youngest person to ever work in the tower, alongside the best scientists in the city.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: This is where I met her.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Tasked with guarding the door to her lab, I got to see her everyday and we grew close.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Sounds like someone had a little crush.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Did you want to hear the story or not?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Sorry, please keep going.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: One night, Clara was working late and made a discovery that would change life in the S.U.N as we know it.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: She had built a machine that carefully extracted a heat unit and could extract triple the amount of light and heat they normally produce.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: She brought it to the council thinking that they’d be excited she found a better way to extract light and heat, but she was wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: The council hid your mother’s discovery and exiled her from the Core, forcing her to live in the outskirts.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: When I found out I rushed to help her and was discharged from the enforcers and exiled, just for association.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: She was exiled for BETTERING the city?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Do any of the council members have a brain!?

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: That was my first reaction too but, in the moment, there was nothing we could do.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: What happened after you guys made it to the outskirts?

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: We started a life out here together.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: When we first arrived the community was unhappy, seeing two people that grew up inside the Core now claiming the outskirts as their home.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: A man named Finn was the first to break the silence.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: He spoke about a movement called “Armada” that opposed the council and the Holy Mother, set on exposing the truth of what truly goes on in that tower.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Finn let us into his home, and we talked for a while, realizing our views aligned he asked us to come to one of their meetings.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: We agreed and met with everyone. With Finn vouching for us the people began to accept us, and we grew closer with people in the community.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: However, no one except Clara knew the truth to why she was exiled.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Clara told me she was caught trying to steal some of the lab equipment…

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: It wasn’t until the day she found out she was pregnant with you she told me the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Clara knew that with you coming into this world she had to do something to make it better.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: We planned for months on the best way to leak your mother’s discovery to the public, without getting killed in the process.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: While we were working you decided you wanted to come out into the world early-- you were always this stubborn.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I just don’t like taking shit from people.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Good to know it started when I was a fetus.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: After a long labour you were born, and Clara got to hold you for the first time.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: I could see it in her face that she would do anything to get her discovery to the public.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: While fetching Clara a drink down the hall, I saw two men suddenly and swiftly wheel her out of the room.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: I started into a sprint, screaming for her but heard no answer.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: The men turned into a room not too far down the hall, but when I ran in, it was empty.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: I never forgave myself for leaving her alone in that room.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: That was the last time anyone saw her.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Let me make sure I heard that correctly. She made a life-changing discovery, and they hid it?

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: We must finish what she started!

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Where’s the machine? And what happened to Armada? Why aren’t they still fighting.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Woah, woah, slow down. I have no idea what happened to that machine.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: As for Armada, they’ve been disbanded.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: What, why?

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: When Clara was went missing it scared a lot of people. Especially the members of Armada.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: They thought that if Clara could disappear so easily then so could they.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: There weren’t enough members left to make any real change but that didn’t stop Finn and I from trying.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: We tried recruiting new members, but no one wanted to get involved.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: After a while we slowly stopped trying and Finn turned into a recluse.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: No one has heard from him in the last 17 years.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Well, if we can’t find him, we can find the machine.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: I’m not sure if you’re ready for this. You have no idea what you are going up against.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: These people don’t care at all about you and won’t think twice about killing you.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I might not know what I’m up against, but you do.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I don’t know where to start, I need your help Kip, please.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: (sighs)

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: This is all your mother’s stuff… Or rather, what’s left of it.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: While in hospital that night, enforcers raided our house and took almost everything.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Thankfully for us, we had a few boxes hidden for that reason exactly.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: I can’t believe this has been here the whole time.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Is this her journal?

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Yes, it is.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Clara used to write all her important notes in there.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: What happened to these pages?

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: We used to rip out pages and plaster them to the walls while working with them…

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: I guess those were taken when they raided the place. They could be anywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Mrs. Watts?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Isn’t that the old lady that lives in our district?

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Yeah, your mother and her used to chat all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Perfect!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: It looks like we found our first lead. There’s no time to waste we have to speak to her.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Calm down, we’re in the late grey zone right now.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: There are enforcers everywhere telling people to stay in their houses.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I can go by myself.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: It’ll be faster, and I can sneak past the guards.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: No! You are NOT allowed to look for this machine.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: And never tell anyone what I just told you.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Remember how I say you NEVER want to get caught out in the midnight zone. There are enforcers, bandits, and things…

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: …you could never imagine, yes, I know.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: You’ve been telling me the same thing since I was a little kid.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Because I never want you to forget.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Trying to find this machine will be much worse and I can’t lose you.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I bet you wouldn’t say this to my mom.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Go to bed now.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: But…

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Now!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I’m going to finish what you started mom, no matter what it takes.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Alright, it’s not that far. Lira, you can do this.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Not a single light on…

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Let me try the back.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Mrs. Watts it’s me Lira Drave.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I have something important to talk to you about.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: It’s about my mom, Clara.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Lira!

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: What are you doing out? You might’ve been seen.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Get inside quick dear!

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Now what is so urgent you couldn't wait for light?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I found out the truth about my mom.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: About her discovery…

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Shhh! Don’t say that too loud or you’ll get us both killed.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: …and about how she disappeared.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I believe that I can finish her work, and you are the only lead I had.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I need to find her machine.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: I haven’t thought about Clara in years.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: We used to work in the tower together until…

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Well, you know what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Do you know anything about the machine she created?

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Of course! I helped her make it.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: She did most of the work, I just assisted in the places she struggled.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Do you know where it is?

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: No, I’m afraid not.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: The last I heard is that someone split it up into three parts.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Three parts?

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Hold on one second.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Now, are you sure you want to be a part of this?

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Once you start, there is no going back.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Yes!

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: I’m hesitant but you’re Clara’s daughter, and if anyone was ready for this it’d be her own.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Please, I promise I’m ready.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Here are the three parts.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: So, you don’t know where any of the parts are?

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Well… I don’t know where they are, but I might know someone who does.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Who?

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: There is an antique shop across the street, owned by a man named Darren.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: He knew your mother.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: So, he shouldn’t have a hard time recognizing who you are.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: All you have to do is get across the street without being seen.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: And hurry, the midnight zone is approaching.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: They’re not moving, how am I supposed to get by?

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: I believe there are a few rocks out front. You can use those to distract the enforcers.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Alright, I’ll go now and make it quick.

dialogues.speaker: Mrs. Watts
dialogues.text: Be smart Lira and be carful who you trust.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Now how do I get in?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Hopefully my luck stays like this.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Clara?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: No, that’s my mother.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: You must be Lira.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Umm…

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: How do you know who I am?

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: You were all Clara talked about before she disappeared.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: She’d talk about how excited she was to have a daughter, and how great it will be getting to see her grow into her own person.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: She kept telling me that a change was coming but wasn’t able to tell me why.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: 20 years and I’m still waiting for that change.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Is that you and my mom?

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Yep.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: That was the day we cleaned out an abandon heat mine and had a small spot away from those fucking enforcers.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Here, take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: She’s beautiful.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Yes, she is.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: And Kip, he looks so young!

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Yeah, I wonder what happened to him.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I think I know what “change” my mom was talking about.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Really?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: This is what my mom was going to use on the tower.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: I recognize this for some reason.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Holy shit!

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Wait right here.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: I know it’s here somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Need any help?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I’ll take that as a no.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Oh my god! You have a piece.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Keep your voice down!

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Yes, I’ve had this in my possession for some time now, but I was never completely sure it’s function.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: All I knew was that Clara wanted me to keep it safe, and I didn’t ask anymore questions.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: But it looks like you can make better use of it.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Thank you, I promise a change is coming.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: You sound just like Clara.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: If you ever need help let me know.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Good luck Lira.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Wait, you can’t leave right now.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: I would hate myself if I let Clara’s daughter out into the midnight zone.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Please stay I have a spare room in the store.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: At least until we’re in the grey zone.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I don’t really know you.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: I promise, anything you find out there will be more dangerous.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I’m not sure.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Can I show you one more thing?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I guess so.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: This was the first time Clara had access to a camera since leaving the Core.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: There are more around her somewhere, but I thought it’d make you feel more comfortable knowing your mom’s stayed in this room before.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: My mom really stayed here?

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Yep.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: She stuck around for all the cool trinkets I have around the shop.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: She used the camera so much I eventually gave it to her.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Better to be put to use than collecting dust on a shelf.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: That’s true.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I guess you’re right about the midnight zone being dangerous.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Also, to make you feel a little bit better the door locks from the inside.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: This is the key for the door.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Keep it in here with you while you sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: Alright, I think it’s late enough. Time for both of us to get some sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Darren
dialogues.text: It was nice meeting you Lira.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Nice meeting you too.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: And it was nice getting to hear more about my mom.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: What time is it?!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Looks like I better get moving.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Alright, one piece down, just two to go.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I’m glad I won’t have to sneak around enforcers on my way home.

dialogues.speaker: Young Girl
dialogues.text: Hey Lira!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Jackie!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: What’ve you two been up to?

dialogues.speaker: Jackie
dialogues.text: Just reading the books you gave us.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Wow! Already reading on your own.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: At this rate you two are going to be able to read books out of my “big kid” collection.

dialogues.speaker: Jackie
dialogues.text: Can you PLEASE come read with us?

dialogues.speaker: Jackie
dialogues.text: Please, please, please?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I’m sorry girls.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Right now, I’m busy.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: But make sure you two find me when you finish your books.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I have many more you’re going to like.

dialogues.speaker: Jackie
dialogues.text: Ok, we will!

dialogues.speaker: Jackie
dialogues.text: Bye Lira!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Bye, be safe!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Oh shit!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I can’t let him see me, he thinks I’m still in my room.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Lira!

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: I didn’t here you get up when did you leave the house?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: When you left the house, it woke me up.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Oh, sorry kid.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: No, no, don’t worry about it.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: What have you been up to?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I’ve just been looking around for Andi. I can’t seem to find him.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: That’s weird. When I left, I passed him walking towards our house.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: He told me he was looking for you.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Someone must’ve distracted him or pulled him away.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Hmm…

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: You know how it is, everyone’s always looking for a second hand.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Yeah, you’re right.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: Well, I’d head that way if you want to find him.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Perfect, thank you!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: When are you going to be home?

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: They asked if I could stay longer in the mines today, but they didn’t really give me a choice.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Aw, ok I’ll see you later.

dialogues.speaker: Kip
dialogues.text: See you later kid.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: That was close.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Let’s hope Andi’s still somewhere around here.

dialogues.speaker: Andi
dialogues.text: Lira!

dialogues.speaker: Andi
dialogues.text: Finally, I’ve been waiting an hour. Where have you been?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Let’s go inside. I got a lot to tell you.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I finally learned something about my mom.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Kip told me a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Andi
dialogues.text: Oh my god, what did he say?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: You can’t say anything, to anyone!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Promise me.

dialogues.speaker: Andi
dialogues.text: I promise.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Ok.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: There was a lot, but she was a scientist working in the Core and figured out a way to turn all eight lights on at once.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: An extraction machine that produces three times the amount of heat and light that they do now.

dialogues.speaker: Andi
dialogues.text: What?!

dialogues.speaker: Andi
dialogues.text: Why does no one know about this!?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: The council hid it when they found out.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: They knew it would be harder for them to stay in power, so they exiled her from the Core to keep her quiet.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Kip tried to help her and got exiled as well.

dialogues.speaker: Andi
dialogues.text: What was Kip doing in the Core?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: You’re not going to believe me, but…

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: He was an enforcer.

dialogues.speaker: Andi
dialogues.text: WHAT!

dialogues.speaker: Andi
dialogues.text: Why has he never mentioned it?

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: He was probably embarrassed, I know I’d be.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I want to finish my mom’s work and turn on all eight lights.

dialogues.speaker: Andi
dialogues.text: That sounds awesome!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: More like how do WE plan on doing that.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I’m going to need your help; you’re my closest friend and one of the two people I trust the most.

dialogues.speaker: Andi
dialogues.text: I was waiting for you to ask.

dialogues.speaker: Andi
dialogues.text: What have you got so far?

dialogues.speaker: Andi
dialogues.text: I can’t believe we knew none of this!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Me too!

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: You’d think in our 19 years of life they would’ve mentioned something.

dialogues.speaker: Andi
dialogues.text: I guess he didn’t want us to have to deal with the consequences of knowing.

dialogues.speaker: Andi
dialogues.text: Anyway, I should get going, midnight zone will be here in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: You’re right.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I’ll see you soon, we’ve got a lot to figure out.

dialogues.speaker: Andi
dialogues.text: You got that right.

dialogues.speaker: Andi
dialogues.text: Bye Lira.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: Hey mom, I know you’re out there somewhere and I hope you can hear me.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: I’m going to finish what your started.

dialogues.speaker: Lira
dialogues.text: No matter the cost.
